name: Raffles Bali
positioning: Hillside villa resort above Jimbaran Bay, where every villa has its own pool and garden, with a private beach and the Rumari restaurant at the resort's highest point
best_for: Travelers who want a private-pool villa with ocean views, a short drive from the airport
Food lovers interested in progressive Indonesian cuisine and a chef's table
Guests who want Balinese rituals and spa treatments on site

facts.text: The resort cascades down a hillside towards the Indian Ocean.
Each villa has its own pool and garden, with views across Jimbaran Bay.
The private limousine transfer from Ngurah Rai International Airport takes less than half an hour.
The restaurant Rumari is set at the highest point of the resort.
At Rumari, chef Gaetan Biesuz presents progressive Indonesian cuisine.
The Writers Bar serves classic and spiced cocktails on a terrace with ocean and sunset views.
The resort has a private beach.
The Sanctuary is a remote hillside treatment suite for signature treatments and wellness journeys.
Spa treatments may be carried out in the privacy of the guest's villa.
The resort has two clay-surface tennis and pickleball courts.
The Raffles Butler arranges a selection of cultural experiences and leisure activities.

highlights.text: The Secret Cave offers dining in a dramatic cave, with flickering torches leading to the table.
The Rumari Counter is a chef's table for up to ten guests where no menu is ever the same.
The Soul Blessing Ceremony is a guided ritual led by a Balinese priest at the resort temple.
The seaside infinity pool looks out to Mount Agung on clear days.
Rumari follows an 80/20 philosophy: 80% of produce is sourced from the Indonesian archipelago and 20% is imported out of necessity.

considerations.text: The resort's hillside in Jimbaran is seeing nearby development, which may occasionally cause daytime noise.
At Rumari, slip-ons and flip-flops are not permitted.
Spa treatments are available for guests aged 12 and above.
